mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods following a UNRATE decrease, or the Rank IC for UNRATE and S&P 500 returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates stronger economic activity, which may lead to higher corporate revenues and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of periods following an INDPRO increase, or the Rank IC for INDPRO and S&P 500 returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates expanding construction activity and economic growth, which may lead to increased demand for related goods and services, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods following a HOUST increase, or the Rank IC for HOUST and S&P 500 returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates a growing economy, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of periods following a GDPC1 increase, or the Rank IC for GDPC1 and S&P 500 returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.1% indicates monetary easing, which may lower borrowing costs and increase investment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods following a FEDFUNDS decrease below 0.1%, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS and S&P 500 returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) combined with an increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods following a simultaneous UNRATE decrease and PAYEMS increase, or the Rank IC for the combination and S&P 500 returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 220 combined with an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.2% indicates tightening monetary conditions, which may lead to decreased investment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of periods following a CPIAUCSL increase above 220 and FEDFUNDS increase above 0.2%, or the Rank IC for the combination and S&P 500 returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which may lead to increased corporate revenues and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, particularly in a late-cycle expansion regime.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods following an RSAFS increase during a late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC for RSAFS and S&P 500 returns is below 0.03.
